html:
Tool and Skill contracts

src/agent_runtime/tools.py defines the only tool contract. A ToolDefinition contains:

Field Runtime purpose
id Globally unique canonical domain.operation ID
display_name, description Human title and model-visible operation description
arguments_schema Complete JSON Schema object, validated before dispatch
result_schema Optional documentation of result data; adapters and their tests own result validation
effect read, write, internal or dynamic; internal Agent state mutations default to no confirmation
state_domain external (default) or internal; local state does not advance external-state revisions and cannot enter execution-cache replay
execution_target Optional gateway or controller execution ownership; Gateway tools receive a selected-ID target enum in multi-Gateway model schemas, extracted before business argument validation
completion_contract Source-owned synchronous (default), managed, or explicit physical completion contract; never supplied by a model or tool argument
resource_class Optional source-owned scheduler demand: lightweight, cpu_heavy, disk_read_heavy, disk_heavy, network_heavy, gpu_heavy, mixed or unknown. It does not grant permission or prove an operation is read-only.
cancellation_transport Optional gpu, local_ai, docker, pdf, office, http, command, email, desktop, clipboard, screen, browser or ui cancellation delivery. Proxmox uses the Gateway HTTP path.
requires_confirmation Additional authorization requirement
availability Prerequisite description in discovery
availability_check Optional deterministic runtime-context check; returns available and a reason when unavailable; excluded from serialization
input_guard Optional deterministic rejection before invocation persistence or schema diagnostics; returns a bounded error without reflecting inputs
authorization_owner, authorization_check Optional named resource-policy authority and its preflight callback. A callback requires an owner; it returns a PolicyBlock or permits the ordinary checks to continue. It does not bypass execution safety.
presentation Optional source-owned capability presentation metadata used by observation/UI consumers
executor Bound deterministic handler returning ExecutionResult; excluded from serialization

A SkillDefinition groups tools with skill_id, display_name, description, availability, platforms and credential_requirements. Nonempty platforms restricts the API runtime using sys.platform values. Gateway target compatibility still belongs to the adapter. The catalog evaluates each tool's local prerequisites from the configured execution context. An unavailable tool remains listed with its reason but contributes no callable schema. Skill availability requires at least one available entry tool (or owned/reused tool when no entries are declared), followed by any skill-level availability check. Inspect individual tool states for mixed families such as Python.

Large skills can declare entry_tool_ids and a SkillSectionDefinition tree. Each section has a stable section_id, direct tool_ids, child section IDs and optional api_path. Validation rejects unknown ownership, duplicate sections, multiply owned children and cycles. Initial preferred-skill exposure and skill discovery use entry tools; section discovery exposes only direct operations and child metadata. Availability summaries also use entry tools for these skills. Skills without entries or sections retain their existing discovery behavior.

Additional skill metadata has separate responsibilities:

Field Responsibility
uses_tools Reuse an already registered operation without creating another execution owner. Registration rejects missing referenced tools.
selection automatic, explicit_only or dependency_only selection mode, plus a bounded routing summary. This does not authorize execution.
instructions, instructions_once, instructions_in_context Source-owned model guidance and its catalog exposure controls. These values are runtime inputs; documentation changes must preserve them.
configuration Source-declared installation configuration schema, defaults and UI fields, persisted through the settings service. Secret fields reference Parameter Store entries; configuration does not grant conversation authority.
resources Resource identities, scope, CRUD classifications and exact tool/action bindings. Missing/unsupported operations remain explicit.
progress Required registration-time progress declaration. Every owned tool must be classified as supported or unsupported; reused tools require explicit delegation. Providers consume existing evidence and report user-facing progress, without entering model discovery.

The registry requires a SkillProgressDefinition even though the model permits None before registration. A skill with no detailed extractor can explicitly use SkillProgressDefinition.unavailable() and supply a useful reason. The contracts live in tools.py, progress/contracts.py and resource_contracts.py; registration is owned by capabilities/registry.py.

default_enabled=false prevents legacy opt-out policy upgrades from adding a new optional skill. Product defaults remain defined by capability policy; registration alone is not enablement. Proxmox VE is the generated API example.

registered means a definition exists. There is no separate package installation state in this registry, so discovery does not invent an installed flag. Missing OAuth or a database profile may produce authentication_required or configuration_required while the service remains available. These flags do not grant authorization or promise remote provider health. Adapters enforce credentials, platform and provider scope at execution too.

result_schema is descriptive metadata for discovery, tooling, tests and developer readability. Tool adapters own validation and normalization of successful output. The generic ExecutionEngine does not validate result data against this schema and does not infer external-effect failure from a schema mismatch. Preserve effect truth even when reporting fails after an external mutation. Adapter contract tests should compare representative successful output with the documented shape.

Registration validates schemas, unique IDs and executable handlers. A package cannot silently replace an existing tool or partially register after a conflict. Historical namespaces and the reserved __ wire separator are rejected for new definitions. Definitions are source-owned. Registry copies and catalog snapshots prevent accidental mutation of advertised JSON.

Adapters can use an existing deterministic service. They return actual observations, errors or scoped durable job references. They cannot call an auxiliary agent to decide the next operation.

ExecutionResult.lifecycle carries the typed OperationLifecycle defined in execution/lifecycle.py. It separates outcome, execution liveness, resource claim, historical effect uncertainty and cleanup. complete describes output coverage; remote_effect_possible describes effects and is not evidence that execution is still running. A normal nonzero shell exit remains a neutral completed outcome.

The engine binds lifecycle evidence to the operation identity at the adapter return boundary. A synchronous return proves that invocation ended; a transport exception does not. Synchronous inspection of an object whose business status is running does not inherit that object's lifetime. Shell/Python execution uses the managed contract and requires process or owned-job evidence. A composite adapter such as gateway.copy uses the explicit contract and supplies its own lifecycle. Adapters that launch continuing external work must opt into managed/explicit ownership and publish correlated observations; a generic success response is insufficient.

Release requires conclusive inactivity (ended or not_started) and a released or absent claim. A failed outcome can release; a successful acknowledgement can still retain ownership. Contradictory or malformed lifecycle facts remain protected. Guards that return before dispatch publish a no-start receipt. Runtime exceptions after dispatch cannot acquire that proof from a worker's failure status.

Scheduling identity is separate from completion evidence. New Namespace V2 profiles capture a pinned Gateway enrollment (or Controller identity), optional physical alias and shared-resource claims before admission. Tool arguments and scheduling hints cannot mint physical identity, erase inferred writes, or waive execution permissions. An opaque program remains marked as externally unresolved under the default target isolation policy. Detected external effects with no usable shared key fail admission with a scope action; they do not reserve a Controller-wide wildcard while waiting.

Every advertised argument must affect execution as documented. Remove historical no-ops; document and reject arguments that do not apply to the selected action. Test observable behavior, including limits, pagination, exact bindings and effect uncertainty.
